title: KMS/HSM rotation + encryption audit pipeline for regional residency & retention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an automated pipeline that ties KMS/HSM key rotation events to an immutable encryption-evidence stream for auditable proofs, plus controls for per-region data residency and retention policies. This ticket covers integrations with cloud KMS providers (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), on-prem HSM connectors (PKCS#11), and the evidence-generation/reporting components consumed by Compliance and Security teams.

Scope:
- Wire rotation lifecycle events (rotate/init/deprecate/revoke) into a central audit stream stored in region-specific evidence buckets with tamper-evident metadata.
- Ensure key rotation triggers cascade actions where required: re-encrypt persisted objects, refresh KV cache signatures, and surface any re-encrypt failures to the ops console.
- Implement retention-aware evidence packaging: retention metadata must reflect data residency (e.g., EU-only evidence) and retention window enforcement.
- Expose an encrypted audit report API and CSV/JSON export for auditors.

Out of scope:
- Full data re-hosting for customers moving residence; separate migration epic.

Design notes / decisions so far:
- Use a signed, append-only evidence record model: each record contains key_id, rotation_epoch, key_thumbprint, rotation_root_hash, service_version, region, and a signed Merkle checkpoint accessible to auditors.
- Rotation orchestration will be implemented as part of the key-manager service: it will call provider SDKs and publish events to the evidence Kafka topic. Evidence topic consumers will materialize compressed proof bundles into region-tagged S3/GCS/Azure storage with server-side encryption configured to the customer's residency region.
- For on-prem HSMs, we will implement a PKCS#11 bridger running in the customer's VPC that forwards signed rotation receipts to the control plane using mTLS.
- Re-encryption strategy: lazy re-encrypt for large datasets + immediate re-encrypt for small critical objects (auth tokens, system secrets). Re-encrypt jobs will be idempotent and track progress with checkpoints to allow safe retries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rotation event -> evidence bundle pipeline end-to-end with >=99% success in staging for both cloud KMS and simulated PKCS#11 HSM connectors.
- Evidence bundles stored in region-tagged buckets and accessible via audit API with read-only keys.
- Automated tests for rotation failure modes and re-encrypt rollback paths.
- Documentation (Confluence) with runbook for manual key revocation and auditor export steps.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gated in staging for internal Redwood tenants.
2) Enable for a pilot customer with EU residency requirement.
3) Monitor re-encrypt job latency, evidence generation success, and storage costs for 2 weeks, then enable for additional regions.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Large re-encrypt jobs could spike network/GPU usage; mitigation: throttled worker pool and lazy re-encrypt heuristics.
- Risk: Proof storage increases S3/GCS costs; mitigation: configurable evidence retention policy and compression.
- Risk: Clock skew affecting signed checkpoints; mitigation: include monotonic rotation_epoch and NTP checks on bridger nodes.

Docs / artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KMS+HSM+Rotation+Audit+Pipeline (draft)
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/58
- Prototype service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/key-manager/tree/rotation-audit-proto

Next steps:
- Build proof-of-concept for PKCS#11 bridger and end-to-end evidence bundle in staging (owner: Liam).
- Create compliance export endpoint spec and a small internal UI in the Console to view bundles (owner: PM).
- Schedule security review with Crypto team after POC (owner: Aisha).
